newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain, France propose 5,000-strong Zaire aid force.
newsitem.headline: Spain, France propose 5,000-strong Zaire aid force.

text.p: Spain and France want to send a multinational force of at least 5,000 troops in a relief effort to open humanitarian corridors for a million starving refugees in Zaire, a foreign ministry spokesman said on Wednesday.
French and Spanish leaders discussed the plan at a summit on Monday and Tuesday in Marseille.
"It is a concrete proposal by France and Spain. In the first phase, the troops will secure humanitarian corridors for food and medicine," said the spokesman who asked not to be named.
A minimum of 5,000 soldiers would be needed for the operation to save refugees deprived of food by fighting between Zairean troops and Rwanda-backed Tutsi rebels, he added.

France would send about 1,000 troops, Spain would send fewer than 1,000 and the two countries hope the United States and other nations would contribute thousands more. But no other nations have committed themselves to sending troops, the spokesman said.
The Franco-Spanish initiative envisages three phases.
"The idea is little by little, the troops will be replaced by Africans," the spokesman said. "In the second phase, it will be international troops with Africans, in the third phase only Africans."
France and Spain are awaiting international backing for sending troops, particularly from the United States but also from the United Nations and the Organisation of African Unity.
With the U.S. election on Tuesday, Washington has not been devoting much attention to the crisis in Africa.
International aid workers have pleaded for urgent world action to avert a humanitarian disaster.

Belgium, Italy and Great Britain may also participate in the multinational force, Spain said. Britain has said it is too early to know if it would join the force but it will discuss the proposal at a summit with France on Friday.
The relief plan faces enormous obstacles already.
Firstly, aid workers in the area say they have lost track of the fleeing refugees' precise whereabouts in eastern Zaire.
Urgently requested satellite photographs to assess the flight, which the United States provided in Bosnia and elsewhere to help humanitarian relief, have failed to materialise.
Meanwhile, time is running out for young, old, weak and ill refugees threatened by hunger, thirst, disease and exposure. Their food supplies are dwindling.

A further complication came on Wednesday when Zaire said it did not want food distributed to the refugees from its soil, insisting it should be done inside the two neighbouring countries Zaire accuses of aggression to encourage refugees to go home.
African diplomats are to meet in Ethiopia to further a plan for a protection force -- on Monday next week.
